quote: If a third party claims or threatens a claim that Materials or Base Components IBM provides to Customer or uses in connection with the performance of the Services infringe that party's patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret, then IBM will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer, its Enterprise and their respective employees, officers, agents and directors against that claim or threatened claim at IBM's expense and pay all costs, damages, penalties and reasonable attorneys' fees that a court finally awards in connection with that claim
rationale: Section 8.1 gives us a Vendor-side IP infringement defence and indemnity covering Materials and Base Components, extended to our Enterprise and personnel, with the standard procedure (prompt notice, IBM control, our cooperation — with IBM reimbursing our cooperation costs) and the usual exclusions (our contributed content, our modifications, combinations with non-IBM products, non-IBM hardware/software/data) and remedies (enable continued use, modify, replace, or credit up to 12 months of charges). That is squarely the playbook fallback position, and Section 9.1(a) carves indemnification payments out of IBM's liability cap, so the indemnity is not squeezed by the general cap — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. Noted but not flagged: 8.1 does not add the preferred non-IP heads (breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the infringement remedy is IBM's "entire obligation", and our indemnity in 8.2 is broader than the preferred Customer-content-only scope (notably 8.2(a)(3) for Services Recipient claims, though partly offset by the carve-back in paragraph c for IBM's misconduct or breach). These are sub-elements/other-rule points, not a failure of this rule's fallback, so no redline here.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We flip the default so that Materials created for us during the Service performance period are Type I (owned by us) rather than Type II, and we confirm that we retain ownership of our Content; our playbook requires that we own the deliverables we pay for and all data we put in, with IBM keeping its pre-existing IP. If IBM prefers, we can instead keep the Type II default provided the Type II licence is expanded to a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense the Materials for our business.

ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.
ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.

ops.text: e. As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and the Customer Components. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content, the Customer Components or any Type I Materials, and no Materials will be jointly owned.

proposal.summary: Default Materials to Type I (Customer-owned) and confirm Customer ownership of Content

quote: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
rationale: Section 7.0 (Materials) defaults all deliverables to Type II Materials, i.e. IBM (or a third party) holds all right, title and interest, and Customer receives only an irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform and distribute copies "within Customer's Enterprise only" (p0085). That fails the preferred position (Customer owns work product created for it, with a licence back for embedded Vendor IP) and also fails the fallback, because the licence back excludes any right to modify/prepare derivative works or to sublicense and is confined to the US portion of our Enterprise per the "Enterprise" definition. The minimal fix is to flip the default to Type I Materials, which already gives Customer full title while granting IBM a broad licence back so IBM retains use of its own know-how and pre-existing Type II IP. Customer Data is not assigned to IBM anywhere ("Content" is defined as Customer-provided and IBM obtains only Required Consents), but there is no express ownership statement, so we add one confirming we retain title to Content and Customer Components and that no Materials are jointly owned.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The caps in Sections 9.1/9.2 are mutual and 12-month based, which works for us, but they currently swallow confidentiality, data protection and security breaches (Section 9.1(c)(2) even excludes data loss entirely) as well as gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. We have added a single mutual carve-out provision so that those items and the Section 8 indemnities sit outside the cap, consistent with our standard position; we are happy to keep the caps themselves as drafted.

ops.text: 9.3 Exclusions from Limitations. Notwithstanding Sections 9.1, 9.2 and 10 (including Subsection 9.1(c)(2)), neither party's liability is limited or excluded in respect of: (a) a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations (including under the AECI); (b) a party's indemnification obligations under Section 8; (c) a party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud; and (d) a party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

proposal.summary: Add mutual carve-outs (confidentiality/data, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) outside the liability caps

quote: c. the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services. The foregoing limit also applies to any of IBM's Affiliates and Subcontractors. It is the cumulative maximum for which IBM and its Affiliates and Subcontractors are collectively responsible. Under no circumstances is IBM, its Affiliates or its Subcontractors liable for any of the following:
rationale: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose substantively identical caps on each party (greater of $100,000 or 12 months' charges paid), and Section 10 excludes consequential damages mutually while preserving Customer's payment obligations — so the cap basis, mutuality and payment-obligation points all satisfy the playbook. Indemnification payments (9.1(a)/9.2(a)) and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the cap. However, the required carve-outs for breach of confidentiality/data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement are absent, and Section 5.4/6.0 expressly makes Sections 9 and 10 prevail over the AECI for confidential information in the hosting environment, while Subsection 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data altogether. That fails the fallback (which requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct) on a material term and is one-sided in IBM's favour. Minimal fix: a single mutual carve-out provision (new Section 9.3) leaving the existing caps intact.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made the assignment provision reciprocal: IBM's assignment now requires our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and cannot be to our competitor, and we have added the standard affiliate/asset-sale carve-out to our side. Our playbook requires at least mutual assignment rights, and as drafted only we were restricted.

ops.newText: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement, without IBM's consent, to an Affiliate or to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets. IBM will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and in no event to a competitor of Customer.
ops.oldText: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition.

proposal.summary: Make § 14.10 mutual: add affiliate/asset-sale carve-out for Customer and a consent requirement on IBM assignment.

quote: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition.
rationale: § 14.10 binds only Customer: we need IBM's consent for assignments (with an M&A successor carve-out), while IBM's own right to assign is entirely unrestricted (and § 14.18 expressly contemplates "assignees of IBM Corp."). That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual right to assign to successors with a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard for other assignments, because there is no consent gate or competitor bar on IBM's side. There is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere in the Agreement, so no walk-away trigger. The redline restores mutuality by requiring our consent (not unreasonably withheld) for IBM assignments and barring assignment to our competitors, and adds the affiliate/asset-sale carve-out on our side to reach the preferred position; the reciprocal consent language alone would be an acceptable fallback.

quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity, sole-supplier, minimum-purchase or requirements commitment on Bluefly. Searches for "exclusive", "sole", "requirements from" and "minimum" surface only warranty-disclaimer, licence-grant ("nonexclusive") and discretion usages, none of which restrict our sourcing. Section 14.16 (Freedom of Action) affirmatively confirms that "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others," and Section 11.5 leaves capacity decisions with us rather than committing volume to IBM. Section 14.11 (No Resale) restricts resale of the Services, which is a downstream distribution restriction, not an exclusive-dealing obligation, and is addressed elsewhere. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity obligation on Customer), so no redline is required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us; where an early-termination charge is unavoidable we cap it at three months' charges as the sole amount due on termination for convenience. As drafted the charge is set in the attachments and is uncapped, so we cannot quantify our exposure.

ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' charges for the terminated Services (calculated using the average monthly charges for such Services over the three (3) months preceding the notice of termination) and will be the sole amount payable by Customer, and IBM's sole remedy, as a result of such termination for convenience.
ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

proposal.summary: Cap early termination charges under Section 3.4(b) at three months' charges and make them the sole termination-for-convenience remedy.

quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
rationale: Section 3.4(b) conditions our termination-for-convenience right on paying "early termination charges" fixed in Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, which are not reproduced or capped in this Agreement. That is a stipulated, Customer-payable termination amount of unknown and potentially unlimited size, so it fails the fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) on a material term. No other Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties appear (Section 3.3 confirms IBM cannot recover these charges where IBM is in breach, and Section 9.2 caps our liability generally); the "late payment fees" reference in Section 4.2 is ordinary interest and is noted only. Redline adopts the fallback: a three-months'-charges cap and sole-remedy wording, since the early-termination charge is part of the bargain for our convenience-termination right.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and limited revocation to our uncured material breach, since our playbook does not accept a licence that is revocable at IBM's discretion or that excludes the group entities and suppliers who actually use the Services. If helpful, we can instead cover Affiliates on written notice to IBM.

ops.newText: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license, revocable only for Customer's uncured material breach and transferable to any successor permitted under Section 14.10, to use the Base Components
ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components

proposal.summary: Extend the Base Components licence to Customer Affiliates and contractors, and remove revocability at will

quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
rationale: The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable" with no stated cause standard, i.e. revocable at IBM's discretion, and it runs to "Customer" only — no Affiliates or contractors acting on our behalf, with no notice mechanism to add them. § 14.17 confirms only expressly specified licences are granted, closing off any implied extension. That combination is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice). Transferability is separately satisfied by § 14.10, which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so our redline only removes revocation at will (limiting it to our uncured material breach) and extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors, with a cross-reference to the permitted successor transfer.

quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds us. § 14.16 "Freedom of Action" is mutual and expressly preserves each party's freedom to enter similar agreements with others, and searches for "compet", "Customer shall not", "develop", "field of use", "territory" and "exclusiv" turn up no restriction on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The only "Customer shall not" provision is § 14.11 No Resale ("Customer shall not resell the Services, in whole or in part."), which is an ordinary limit on redistributing IBM's own Services rather than a restraint on our business, and § 13.2 (Acceptable Use Policy) governs use of the Services only. This meets the preferred position of no non-compete restriction on Customer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we may terminate for convenience without penalty and with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges; as a compromise we accept the Attachment A early termination charges capped at three (3) months' recurring Charges, so that an uncapped, undefined charge cannot make this right illusory. We have also added the refund of Charges prepaid for periods after termination, since we should not pay for Services we do not receive.

ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such early termination charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, an amount equal to three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services.
ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

ops.text: IBM will refund to Customer, within thirty (30) days of the termination date, any Charges prepaid by Customer for Services attributable to any period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.summary: Cap early termination charges at three months' recurring Charges and add pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges on convenience termination.

quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
rationale: Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience right on one month's written notice (within the preferred 30-day notice window) and IBM has no convenience right anywhere in the Agreement (§ 3.3 is breach-only), which meets the preferred position on those two material terms. However, § 3.4(b) conditions the right on paying "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" with no cap and no visible schedule, and § 3.5 makes all accrued amounts due with no refund of prepaid Charges. An uncapped, externally-defined exit penalty fails the fallback's cap of three months' fees and can render the convenience right illusory. Redline caps the charges at three months' recurring Charges (fallback level, proportionate given the Attachment A facilities-services bargain) and adds the pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges from the preferred position.

quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
rationale: Searches for audit, inspection, verification, records, usage-monitoring and premises-access language return nothing: the Agreement grants IBM no right to audit or verify Customer's usage, no right to inspect our books or premises, and no access to Customer systems. The only adjacent right is § 11.3, where IBM may "investigate potential violations" of the Customer content warranties, but that is an internal determination by IBM leading to its own remedies — it imposes no audit, on-site inspection or system-access obligation on us, so there is nothing for the audit parameters (frequency, notice, cost) to constrain. The position is therefore better than the preferred position and no redline is warranted. Noted only for the record: § 11.3's final paragraph requires Customer to provide relevant information about events that could lead to a claim against IBM at IBM's request; that is a claims-cooperation duty rather than an audit right, and is a minor sub-element handled under indemnity cooperation rather than this rule.

quote: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
rationale: § 14.3 selects the substantive laws of the State of New York, which is our preferred governing law. The document contains no arbitration provision (no hits for "arbitration") and no foreign or vendor-home-jurisdiction forum, so there is no walk-away risk. The only shortfall is that the clause is silent on venue rather than conferring exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County; with New York law chosen and no competing forum selection, disputes default to courts of competent jurisdiction, so this is a minor sub-element short of the preferred wording and is noted rather than redlined. Related provisions (§ 14.4 jury waiver, § 14.14 limitations period) are noted only and not flagged under this rule.

quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
rationale: No most-favoured-nation obligation is imposed on Customer anywhere in the agreement. Searches for "no less favo(u)rable", "most favored", "best price", "discount" and "any other customer" returned nothing, and the pricing provision (§ 4.1 Charges, p0052) simply provides that Charges are set out in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms, with no obligation on us to extend IBM terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers. § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) expressly confirms each party may enter into similar agreements with others, which is the opposite of an MFN burden on us. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer); no MFN in our favour is granted either, but the rule does not require one, so no redline is warranted.

quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
rationale: The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, committed volume, take-or-pay obligation or shortfall charge on Bluefly. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "take or pay", "shortfall", "volume" and "purchase" return nothing of that character: § 4.1 prices Charges only for Services actually ordered under Service Option Attachments/Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), § 11.5 addresses capacity planning rather than committed capacity, and § 12.3 confirms no goods are purchased. Bluefly also has a monthly termination-for-convenience right on one month's notice (§ 3.4) plus a no-charge exit if IBM changes the Services (§ 13.1), so there is no locked-in multi-year spend. This meets the preferred position (fees for usage/ordered services only). Two points to note but not redline: § 3.4(b) preserves "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments", and § 3.2 auto-renews each Service Option Attachment for a like term absent 90 days' notice — the attachments should be checked to confirm they contain no minimum-volume or take-or-pay pricing, which would be assessed under this rule when available.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: Each party is responsible for the supervision, direction, and control of its respective personnel. IBM reserves the right to determine the assignment of its personnel.
rationale: The agreement contains no non-solicitation or no-hire restriction on Customer. The likely home for such a covenant, § 14.8 (Personnel), addresses only supervision, assignment and subcontracting, and § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) expressly preserves each party's freedom to contract with others; searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ or engage" and "induce" returned no restrictive covenant. This matches the preferred position (no non-solicit binding Customer), so no redline is required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window from 90 to 30 days, fixed renewal terms at 12 months rather than repeating a potentially multi-year term, and added a 60-day renewal reminder plus a cap on renewal price increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, consistent with our playbook position that renewals be easy to exit and predictably priced. If helpful, we can accept a 60-day notice window and a 5% uplift cap as a fallback.

ops.newText: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term of twelve (12) months unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment. IBM will notify Customer in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term of the upcoming renewal and of any proposed change in Charges. Charges for any renewal term will not increase by more than the lesser of (i) the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%) of the Charges for the then-current term.
ops.oldText: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.

proposal.summary: Cap renewal term at 12 months, shorten non-renewal notice to 30 days, add vendor renewal reminder and renewal price uplift cap

quote: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.
rationale: § 3.2 auto-renews each Service Option Attachment for a term equal in duration to the previous term (so a multi-year initial term auto-renews multi-year, which is walk-away territory) and requires 90 days' non-renewal notice, well beyond the fallback ceiling of 60 days. There is also no renewal price predictability: § 4.1 and the rest of the Agreement contain no cap on renewal Charge increases and no renewal reminder. The clause therefore fails the fallback on renewal term length, notice window, and uplift. Redline sets 12-month renewals, a 30-day opt-out window, a 60-day IBM reminder, and a CPI/3% uplift cap; a 60-day window with a 5% cap remains an acceptable fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement currently addresses only accrued payment obligations on termination, with no right to transition assistance or return of our Content. We have added our standard exit provision: up to six months' transition assistance at IBM's then-current rates, return of Content in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. We can work with 90 days of transition assistance if six months is an issue.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Content and other Customer data in its possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Content and Customer data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance, Content return and certified deletion obligations in § 3.5

quote: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.
rationale: This is a hosting/services agreement in which IBM holds our Content, so the playbook expects an exit clause. Section 3.5 (Effect of Termination) addresses only accrued payment obligations, and no transition, exit, data return/export or deletion language exists anywhere in the document (searches for transition, return, export, delete/destroy and migration returned nothing; §§ 11.6 and 14.18 address Customer responsibility for Content and contact-data processing only, and § 14.2 merely lists 3.5 as surviving). The Agreement therefore fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export) and leaves us exposed to loss of Content on termination. We inserted the preferred model language into § 3.5 — six months' transition assistance at IBM's then-current rates, 30-day return in machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter — with the 90-day fallback flagged in the comment.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Materials with a repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, and carved the express warranty out of the "AS IS" disclaimer, since Section 5.1 currently gives us no conformance warranty or remedy at all. Our playbook position is 12 months for software and 90 days for services; we have proposed the 90-day fallback here.

ops.text: c. for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable and all Materials provided by IBM will conform in all material respects to the applicable documentation and specifications and will be free of any virus, malicious or disabling code. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 5.1 is, at IBM's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Deliverable or Materials, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services, Deliverable or Materials.

ops.newText: c. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1, IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES
ops.oldText: c. IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES

proposal.summary: Add a 90-day conformance/no-malicious-code warranty with repair, replace, re-perform or refund remedy, and carve the express warranty out of the "AS IS" disclaimer.

quote: a. it will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill and in accordance with the applicable Service Option Attachments (which means the degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession with respect to work of a similar nature); and that it will provide Customer with competent, fully trained, fully qualified and responsible personnel to perform the Services; and
rationale: Section 5.1 gives a workmanlike-standard services warranty and a compliance-with-laws covenant, which matches part of the preferred position, but it contains no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no warranty period, no no-malicious-code warranty, and no stated remedy (repair, replace, re-perform or refund). Section 5.4(c) then puts all Materials on an unqualified "AS IS" basis, so the disclaimer swallows any implied conformance obligation, and 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive. That fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) on material terms, so we have inserted a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty with the standard remedy and carved the express warranty out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. Support/maintenance under 11.1 and 12.2 is discretionary ("as reasonably determined by IBM") and does not supply an equivalent warranty remedy.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM hosts our environment and processes our Content and personal information, but the Agreement contains no insurance requirement, so we have added a standard provision (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request). If helpful, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

ops.text: IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000, covering IBM's handling of Content and of personal information processed by IBM on Customer's behalf; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 14.12A requiring IBM to maintain CGL, professional liability (E&O) and cyber liability insurance, with certificates on request.

quote: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
rationale:
The Agreement contains no insurance clause anywhere: a full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the section outline has no insurance heading. The nearest risk-allocation provisions (§ 14.12 Risk of Loss, § 5.3 Security) address allocation of loss and security features but impose no obligation on IBM to carry coverage.

IBM is squarely within the rule's scope: it operates the e-business Hosting Environment, holds "Content" (defined at p0017 as the information, software and data Customer provides), and under § 14.18 processes personal information on Customer's behalf. A hosting vendor that processes personal data with no insurance at all is the rule's walk-away scenario, not merely a shortfall against the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M), so this is a "missing" finding requiring insertion.

Redline inserts a new § 14.12A adjacent to Risk of Loss at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request. I used the document's own defined term "Content" plus the § 14.18 personal-information language rather than the playbook's "Customer Data", which is not a defined term in this agreement. The obligation runs against IBM only and does not create any burden on our party. The comment offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback as a landing zone. Severity is low.
